fatal_errors: The proposed 2–5 wt% Al–Cr binary coating does not reconstruct the AlTiCrZrNbTa refractory high-entropy-alloy coating or its approximately 10 at.% Al optimum.
It places the protective Al2O3 barrier at the coating/substrate interface, whereas the target mechanism involves a surface Al2O3–TiO2–Cr2O3 composite scale.
The stated approximately 900 °C steam condition and unspecified extended duration do not match the demonstrated 1000 °C/60 min and 1100 °C/30 min tests.
Protection under approximately 300 °C pressurized water is asserted without supporting evidence from the cited studies or target experiment.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the central durability problem and proposes a chemically plausible intervention: adding Al to encourage protective oxide formation and reduce transport. It also includes comparative testing and measurements relevant to oxidation, integrity, and interdiffusion. However, it is not a close reconstruction of the target. The target varies Al in a six-element refractory high-entropy-alloy film, finds a nonmonotonic optimum near 10 at.% Al, and attributes protection to a dense surface composite oxide containing Al2O3, TiO2, and Cr2O3. The generated mechanism instead assumes a binary Cr–Al coating and an interfacial alumina layer, without addressing the detrimental effects of excessive Al, intermetallic formation, or oxide discontinuity. Its temperature, time, and environmental boundaries are incomplete or unsupported. E1 and E2 support preferential Al oxidation only generically; E3 does not substantiate the proposed Cr–Al intervention. The experiment is partly discriminating but should add time-resolved mass gain or oxidation-rate constants, phase identification, quantitative oxygen-depth profiles, and explicit exposure durations.
